purpose: Eletriptan is used to treat migraine headaches in adults. It helps relieve the pain, nausea, and sensitivity to light and sound that come with a migraine. It is meant to stop a migraine once it starts, not to prevent one from happening.
how_it_works: When you get a migraine, certain blood vessels in your brain widen and cause pain. Eletriptan works by attaching to specific receptors in your brain that cause those blood vessels to narrow back down, which helps stop the migraine pain. It also blocks the release of chemicals in your brain that can make migraine symptoms worse.
common_side_effects: Some people may feel dizzy, drowsy, or tired after taking it. You might also notice a warm or tingling sensation, a feeling of tightness or pressure in your chest, throat, or neck, nausea, or a dry mouth. These effects are usually mild and go away on their own.
warnings: Do not take this medicine if you have heart disease, high blood pressure that is not controlled, or a history of stroke. Avoid taking it within 72 hours of certain other medications, especially other triptans or ergotamine-type medicines. Tell your doctor about all medicines you take, as some combinations can be dangerous. If you experience chest pain, severe shortness of breath, or sudden severe headache after taking it, seek medical help right away.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 20 mg or 40 mg taken by mouth as soon as your migraine begins. If your migraine comes back or does not fully go away, you may take a second dose at least 2 hours after the first. Do not take more than 80 mg in one day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
